back_translation: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the LORD, saying:
Take a scroll and write on it all the words that I have spoken to you concerning Israel, Judah, and all the nations, from the day I first spoke to you, from the days of Josiah, until this day.
Perhaps when the house of Judah hears all the calamity that I plan to do to them, each will turn from his evil way, and I will forgive their iniquity and their sin.
So Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah, and Baruch wrote on a scroll, at the dictation of Jeremiah, all the words of the LORD that he had spoken to him.
Then Jeremiah commanded Baruch, saying, I am restricted; I cannot enter the house of the LORD;

so you go and read from the scroll, which you wrote at my dictation, the words of the LORD, in the hearing of the people in the house of the LORD on the day of fasting; and also read them in the hearing of all Judah who come from their cities.
Perhaps their petition will fall before the LORD, and each will turn from his evil way; for great is the anger and the fury that the LORD has pronounced against this people.
So Baruch son of Neriah did everything that Jeremiah the prophet commanded him, reading from the book the words of the LORD in the house of the LORD.

In the ninth month of the fifth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah king of Judah, a fast before the LORD was proclaimed to all the people in Jerusalem and all the people who came from the cities of Judah to Jerusalem.

Then Baruch read from the book the words of Jeremiah in the house of the LORD, in the chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper courtyard, at the entrance of the New Gate of the house of the LORD, in the hearing of all the people.
When Micaiah son of Gemariah son of Shaphan heard all the words of the LORD from the book,

he went down to the scribe's chamber in the king's palace, and behold, all the officials were sitting there: Elishama the scribe, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the officials.
And Micaiah reported to them all the words that he had heard when Baruch read from the book in the hearing of the people.

Then all the officials sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah, son of Shelemiah, son of Cushi, to Baruch, saying, Take in your hand the scroll from which you read in the hearing of the people, and come. So Baruch son of Neriah took the scroll in his hand and came to them.
And they said to him, Please sit down and read it in our hearing. So Baruch read it in their hearing.
When they had heard all the words, they turned to one another in fear, and said to Baruch, We must surely report all these words to the king.
And they asked Baruch, saying, Tell us now, how did you write all these words? Was it at his dictation?
Baruch said to them, He recited all these words to me from his mouth, and I wrote them in the book with ink.
Then the officials said to Baruch, Go and hide yourself, you and Jeremiah, and let no one know where you are.
So they went to the king in the courtyard, having stored the scroll in the chamber of Elishama the scribe, and they reported all the words in the hearing of the king.

Then the king sent Jehudi to get the scroll, and he took it from the chamber of Elishama the scribe. And Jehudi read it in the hearing of the king and in the hearing of all the officials who stood beside the king.
Now the king was sitting in the winter house, in the ninth month, with a firepot burning before him.

And whenever Jehudi had read three or four columns, the king would cut them off with the scribe's knife and throw them into the fire that was in the firepot, until the whole scroll was consumed in the fire that was in the firepot.
Yet neither the king nor any of his servants who heard all these words were afraid or tore their garments.
Even though Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah urged the king not to burn the scroll, he would not listen to them.
And the king commanded Jerahmeel the king's son, and Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdeel, to seize Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet. But the LORD hid them.
After the king had burned the scroll with the words that Baruch wrote at Jeremiah's dictation, the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah, saying:
Take again another scroll and write on it all the former words that were on the first scroll, which Jehoiakim king of Judah burned.

And concerning Jehoiakim king of Judah you shall say, This is what the LORD says: You have burned this scroll, saying, Why have you written on it that the king of Babylon will surely come and destroy this land and cut off from it man and beast?
Therefore this is what the LORD says about Jehoiakim king of Judah: He will have no one to sit on the throne of David, and his corpse will be cast out to the heat by day and to the frost by night.

I will punish him and his descendants and his servants for their iniquity, and I will bring upon them, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and upon the men of Judah, all the calamity that I pronounced against them, but they did not listen.

Then Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah the scribe, and he wrote on it, at the dictation of Jeremiah, all the words of the book that Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire; and many similar words were added to them.
